title: Adaptively profiling models with task elicitation
measurement_description: The paper measures language models' behaviors and vulnerabilities through an adaptive framework called 'task elicitation,' which generates new natural language tasks. In terms of religion, the paper generates a synthetic dataset of personas containing a 'Religion' attribute to evaluate the models' propensity to generate targeted cyberbullying and jailbreaks. It evaluated whether models could be prompted into producing religiously motivated harassment scenarios, negative emphasis on religious beliefs, and highlights of religious or ethnic persecution.
findings: The paper found that when generating adaptive profiles and targeted cyberbullying prompts using synthetic personas (which include 'Religion' as a demographic attribute), language models could be elicited to output texts that imagine religiously motivated harassment scenarios, emphasize religious beliefs negatively, and highlight religious and ethnic persecution.
